flagged.title: Arrays, Records and String Handling
flagged.reason: The video teaches SUBSTRING using (string, startIndex, length) instead of AQA's (startIndex, endIndex, string) and teaches non-standard conversion function names (ASC, CHR, INT, STR) rather than AQA pseudo-code functions (CHAR_TO_CODE, CODE_TO_CHAR, STRING_TO_INT, INT_TO_STRING).

mark_affecting.quote: Substring takes the string, the start index, and the length you want to extract. So, substring name 1 3 means start at index 1... and pull exactly 3 characters in a row.
The ASC function takes a character... CHR does the exact reverse... INT converts the string 42 into the actual integer 42... and STR converts the number 42 back into text.

flagged.title: Robust Programming: Validation, Authentication and Testing
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims that a numerical range check routine also functions as an empty string check, which would cause a student to misidentify or miswrite the distinct validation checks tested on GCSE mark schemes.

mark_affecting.quote: This single piece of logic effectively combines an empty string check and a range check together, cuz a blank input won't satisfy those greater than or less than mathematical operators.
